message: No detected untrusted source handling: The code fetches models and data from a GitHub repo via dvc.api without any checksum verification, pinned commit/revision, or authentication checks.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training or data preparation.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The data preparation code applies log-transforms and MinMax scaling but includes no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs against poisoning.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads pickled model artifacts from a public GitHub repo via dvc.api without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision to verify integrity before deserializing.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, validates the expected label set, or detects anomalous label distributions before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no activation-pattern analysis, trigger detection, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The model is trained with a standard sklearn AdaBoostClassifier with no differential privacy library or DP-SGD mechanism applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness libraries (Foolbox, ART, etc.) or attack methods (FGSM, PGD) are imported or used anywhere in the evaluation pipeline.

No detected metric tampering protection: While train/test splitting is performed, there is no isolation guarantee (the scaler is fit on test data in process_data), no hashing/signing of evaluation data, and no independent metric verification mechanism.
No detected output bounds checks: The inference path returns model scores directly with no NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or output sanity validation.
No detected prompt injection defenses: The model is a tabular AdaBoost classifier, not an LLM, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
